description: We EXPLORE We ANALYSE We CODE We BUILD
summary:
Instant 708-hour topocentric illumination, LOLA terrain horizon masking, and Direct-to-Earth communication evaluator for Artemis and CLPS lunar landing site selection.

Memorable Project Identity: SeleneSight connects the ancient Greek goddess of the Moon (Selene) with forward-looking situational awareness (Sight).
Defines the Exact Scientific Scope: Immediately informs evaluators that the project solves the dual challenges of the lunar south pole: solar power availability and direct radio communication line-of-sight.
Aligns with NASA Objectives: Explicitly highlights real exploration needs: topocentric horizon profiling for Artemis and CLPS missions using NASA LOLA terrain and JPL Horizons orbital geometry.
details:
Project Details

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

SeleneSight is an interactive, browser-native flight dynamics and mission evaluation platform designed to solve one of the most pressing operational challenges of the Artemis era: rapid topocentric illumination, solar power, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication assessment at the Lunar South Pole.

Because the Moon’s rotational axis is tilted only 1.54∘1.54^\circ1.54∘ relative to the ecliptic, the Sun never rises high into the sky near the lunar poles—it skims the horizon in a continuous 360∘360^\circ360∘ circle over a 29.53-day (708708708-hour) synodic cycle. Even modest crater walls cast razor-sharp, 20 km20\text{ km}20 km shadows that plunge landing sites into prolonged sub-cryogenic darkness. Concurrently, lunar optical libration (±6.68∘\pm6.68^\circ±6.68∘ in latitude and ±7.90∘\pm7.90^\circ±7.90∘ in longitude) causes the Earth to continuously nod and wag, intermittently dropping behind mountainous massifs and severing radio communications with NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN).

How it works:

  • Astronomical Engine: Implements Jean Meeus Astronomical Algorithms to calculate topocentric solar and Earth azimuth and elevation vectors, sub-solar coordinates drifting at the mean synodic rate (∼0.5079∘/hr\sim0.5079^\circ/\text{hr}∼0.5079∘/hr), and bounded optical librations.
  • Terrain Shadow Occlusion: Evaluates line-of-sight clearance against 12-sector azimuthal horizon elevation masks derived from NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) digital elevation models, factoring in geometric vacuum horizon dip (δ=2h/Rmoon\delta = \sqrt{2h / R_{\text{moon}}}δ=2h/Rmoon​​) for elevated rover masts.
  • Photovoltaic Yield Modeling: Computes instantaneous solar flux (1,361 W/m2×η1,361\text{ W/m}^2 \times \eta1,361 W/m2×η) across three solar array geometries: Vertical Cylindrical Mast, 2-Axis Sun-Tracking, and Horizontal Deck Arrays.
  • Flight Dynamics Visualizers: Renders dynamic dual-vector elevation curves, 360∘360^\circ360∘ Polar Dome Reticle Skyplots, Cartesian Linear Panoramas, and real-time transition countdown clocks for next Sunset, Sunrise, Earthset (LOS), and Earthrise (AOS).
  • Scenario Comparator: Performs comparative trade-off analyses between candidate sites (e.g., Shackleton Rim vs. Malapert Massif), calculating differential sunlit hours, communication resilience, and viability scores.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Instant Client-Side Evaluation: Replaces complex, multi-gigabyte desktop GIS software and command-line SPICE toolkit scripts with a zero-latency, browser-based evaluator that generates a full 708708708-hour synodic cycle in milliseconds.
  • Rapid Landing Site Selection: Allows mission architects to immediately identify simultaneous "Golden Windows" where solar power generation and Direct-to-Earth line-of-sight overlap.
  • Dual-Audience Utility: Offers a high-density, monospaced telemetry console for aerospace planners alongside plain-language science tooltips for educators, students, and public explorers.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

  • De-Risking Artemis & CLPS Operations: Aids in identifying landing zones that maximize solar array energy harvesting while ensuring uninterrupted communication links during critical surface traverses into cryogenic Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs).
  • Democratizing Planetary Flight Dynamics: Makes NASA and CSA open planetary science accessible to students, academic institutions, and independent researchers without requiring specialized workstation licenses.

4. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Were Used?

  • Languages & Architecture: Pure browser-native ECMAScript 2022 (JavaScript), HTML5 Canvas 2D API, and CSS3.
    • NASA LOLA (LRO): Gridded topography and azimuthal horizon elevation masks.
    • NASA JPL Horizons: Topocentric orbital vectors and libration calibration.
    • NASA LROC QuickMap & NASA Moon Trek: High-resolution morphological and slope validation.
    • Canadian Space Agency (CSA): Mission context for autonomous surface rover navigation and Canadarm3 orbital servicing.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance: A custom assertion test harness (tests/runAll.js) running 460 automated assertions across 15 test files with a 100% pass rate, coupled with headless browser verification scripts.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

  • Authentic Aerospace Aesthetic: Explicitly rejects cartoonish, generic "vibe-coded" SaaS templates in favor of a specialized Lunar Basalt & Solar Grazing Amber design system (#08090c basalt floor, #f59e0b solar amber, #10b981 avionics green, #ef4444 shadow crimson) featuring high data density, monospaced typography, and zero emojis.
  • Dual Geometric Projections: Offers dual-perspective spatial awareness through both a 360∘360^\circ360∘ circular polar zenith reticle and an unwrapped 0∘–360∘0^\circ\text{–}360^\circ0∘–360∘ linear horizon panorama with real-time scrubbers.
  • Dynamic Trade-Off Scoring: Employs an automated multi-criteria viability model: Viability Score=0.45⋅(Sunlit %)+0.35⋅(DTE %)−0.20⋅(Slope Penalty)\text{Viability Score} = 0.45 \cdot (\text{Sunlit \%}) + 0.35 \cdot (\text{DTE \%}) - 0.20 \cdot (\text{Slope Penalty})Viability Score=0.45⋅(Sunlit %)+0.35⋅(DTE %)−0.20⋅(Slope Penalty)

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Astronomical & Physical Rigor: Bounded draconic and anomalistic libration wobbles, seasonal sub-solar latitude oscillations, exact synodic drift (0.507948∘/hr0.507948^\circ/\text{hr}0.507948∘/hr), and continuous [0∘,360∘)[0^\circ, 360^\circ)[0∘,360∘) azimuth wrapping to eliminate floating-point edge singularities.
  • Hardware & Terrain Realities: Horizon depression due to observer mast elevations, crater-wall shadow cast lengths under grazing angles <1.5∘<1.5^\circ<1.5∘, and Lambertian cosine projection losses on horizontal rover surfaces.
  • Accessibility & Longevity: Guaranteed cross-device accessibility by enforcing zero runtime dependencies, static client-side computation, and transparent open-source code architecture with clean Git modularity.
